title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
An AI image generation system was used to create non-consensual sexual imagery of a real person. The person obtained source photographs from the victim's social media without permission and used the AI tool to generate explicit images that did not exist. He then distributed the synthetic content through multiple anonymous accounts across social media platforms.

The failure was in deployment without safeguards. The AI system had no requirement to verify consent from people depicted in source images, no mechanism to block generation of sexual content involving identifiable individuals, and no auditing of outputs. A system designed to generate images was made available to users with no technical barrier to this use case.

It is not established what specific AI tool was used, what technical measures if any existed within it, or whether the platform policies of the services through which images were shared had detected or removed the content before investigation began.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and sharing obscene AI-generated images of a college acquaintance. Bansal allegedly obtained photographs from the woman's private social media account and used artificial intelligence technology to create fake explicit images. He then distributed this content through multiple fake accounts on Instagram, Discord, and Facebook while maintaining anonymity using various Gmail addresses. The 22-year-old victim discovered the harassment when she received messages from anonymous accounts informing her that morphed photographs and videos were circulating online, along with threatening messages intended to humiliate her.

Police launched an investigation after the woman filed a complaint at the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi. Officers analyzed digital footprints, social media accounts, and email addresses to identify the perpetrator. During interrogation, Bansal admitted he knew the victim from college and that personal conflict between them had motivated his actions. He revealed that after initially uploading the content, other online users created additional explicit AI-generated material that he subsequently reposted. Police recovered a mobile phone, two SIM cards, and other digital evidence connected to the case, with investigations ongoing.
